Episodes 1 to 13 of 18 are authored: 1186 entities, 5,623 exact mentions in original-en and 5,663 in modern-en, 1184 of the 1186 bound in the older edition and 1181 in the modern one, 138 focused tests passing, content revision 2026-09-16.13. NEXT: episode 14 (Oxen of the Sun, 65 paragraphs), the lying-in hospital in Holles street. 2,459 paragraphs remain; the long ones are 15 (Circe, 1,441) and 17 (Ithaca, 654); episode 18 (Penelope) is eight paragraphs of monologue and will be the densest in the book.

EPISODE 13 FOUND THE WORST SOURCE DEFECT IN THE BOOK SO FAR, AND IT IS IN THE MODERN EDITION. A BOTCHED GLOBAL REPLACEMENT OF O WITH OH HAS CORRUPTED FOUR PROPER NAMES AND ONE ABBREVIATION, ALL INSIDE EPISODE 13: doctor OH'HARE at 13:98, OH'HARA'S tower at 13:115, poor man OH'CONNOR at 13:116, Canon OH'HANLON at 13:130, and 'Care of P. OH. Dolphin's Barn' at 13:110. The same edition prints Canon O'Hanlon correctly fifteen times in the same episode and mangles him once. Canon O'Hanlon now carries Oh'Hanlon as a second alias and the other two men are bound by phrases that accept either spelling, so no card is lost -- but this is a TEXT CORRUPTION, NOT A MODERNISATION, and the release owner should see it. No edition byte was touched.

THE GLOSS HABIT IS NOW A PATTERN AND SHOULD BE CHECKED IN EVERY REMAINING EPISODE: the modern edition interpolates parentheses Joyce did not write. 'Henry Flower (Bloom's pen name)' twice in episode 11, 'the Citizen (the nationalist)' SEVENTY TIMES in episode 12, and 'Howth (the headland)' four times in episode 13. A one-line census finds them: look for a parenthesis in the modern paragraph that is absent from the older one.

NAMESAKE SPLITS MADE IN EPISODE 13: bare TOMMY is Tommy Moore at 8:121 and 12:172, Tom Rochford at 10:221 and Tommy Tittlemouse at 15:554, so the twin is keyed and only 'Tommy Caffrey' is aliased; bare JACKY is Jacky Tar at 12:380; REGGY at 8:174 is another Reggy entirely; CUMMINS at 13:71 is Miss Cummins, author of The Lamplighter, and NOT the Cummins of Francis street cast one episode earlier -- two people an episode apart, which is exactly what the occurrence sweep is for. PETER at 13:60 is BLOOM, whom Cissy Caffrey calls 'my uncle Peter over there'.

EXTEND, DO NOT DUPLICATE, CAUGHT THREE TIMES HERE: FLOEY at 13:110 is the Floey Dillon already on the page from episode 6; 'her father' at 13:36 is the gerty-father of episode 10; and S. BERNARD of the procession of saints in episode 12 is the saint Bernard whose prayer of Mary is preached at Sandymount. All three cards were extended and no second card was written.

A KEY THAT LOOKED RIGHT AND WAS NOT: 13:20 says Gerty was 'more a Giltrap than a MacDowell', which is the FAMILY name and not grandpapa Giltrap. The test written in episode 12 caught it. 13:24 and 13:37 are the man and are keyed.

THE LONGEST-SPAN RULE CAN SWALLOW A CARD: a phrase for 'Gabriel Conroy's brother' at 13:111 took the whole span and dropped Gabriel Conroy's own mention. It is a lookbehind now -- (?<=Gabriel Conroy’s )brother -- so both men bind. WATCH FOR THIS whenever a phrase contains a name that is already aliased.

STANDING RULES, UNCHANGED: key by default and alias only on proof; run the whole-book occurrence list on every alias as well as every key; read the omittedEntities line of the validation report on every build, because it is what reports an alias that matches nothing (the italic trap) and an entity whose keys were shadowed; never re-declare a SPLIT or PHRASE literal, merge into the existing one. The build now takes about twenty minutes of CPU for both editions; run it in the background and wait on the log. This lane never sets appStatus.
